### Workflow handoff: urlshort-slice@1 step design_review

Workflow instance: 01M3ZA8Q39QEB3R1QDQCVTER18
Prior step: design (design) closed by design-agent@urlshort-factory
This step: design_review (design_review)
Objective: Independent review of design.md (and impact-analysis.md on brownfield slices) against the SPEC: every acceptance criterion reachable, error contract explicit, data model and migration reversible, threat model covering every new entry point, smallest structure that satisfies the SPEC. MUST-FIX or HIGH routes back to design; otherwise the locked set proceeds to plan_lock.

Prior step note: Re-review candidate d0521de on main, supersedes 3931c8b; SPEC unchanged at 4e581cc. DR-01: fixed, not disputed. Cause accepted: Boot loads a single classpath application.properties and the functional suite's copy shadows the shipped one, so the earlier one-line deletion could not restore ECS logging or problem-details enablement. Replacement mechanism: the suite's override moves to src/functionalTest/resources/application-functional.properties (datasource lines only) and the functionalTest block of build.gradle.kts sets systemProperty spring.profiles.active=functional, so the shipped file is the base and the profile layers on top. Verified by effect on the real functional runtime classpath with a variant of the reviewer's probe: spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true, logging.structured.format.console=ecs and the in-memory H2 datasource with the profile; the shipped file-DB URL without it. Evidence at missions/00-hello/slices/01-ping/design-probe/output.txt, rerunnable with the init script beside it. AC-5 and AC-6 assertions unchanged; the fail-on-non-JSON rule for AC-6 stands; the per-class override fallback is withdrawn. Territory for both new paths granted by the lead at 2b29248; no open territory item; no decision parked on human@kernel. Response recorded in design.md section 11, Self-check updated (row 10, every finding answered); ADR-0004 and docs/DESIGN.md section 4 carry the rule that suite overrides are profile files, never a suite-level application.properties. Follow-up noted for the lead: the unit suite's application.properties shadows the same way.
